segments.text: Episode one hundred and fourteen. Next stop... the Hubble tension.
The universe is expanding. Galaxies are moving away from each other. But how fast?
segments.headline: How fast?

segments.text: That speed is called the Hubble constant. And there are two main ways to measure it.
segments.headline: The Hubble constant

segments.text: Method one: study the oldest light in the universe, and predict how fast space should grow today. Answer: about sixty-seven.
Method two: measure distances to nearby galaxies using special stars and exploding stars. Answer: about seventy-three.
That might sound close. But both are so precise that they shouldn't disagree like this.
segments.headline: They shouldn't disagree

segments.text: The Webb telescope has re-checked the star measurements. Some teams still get seventy-three, others get about seventy.
segments.headline: Webb checks

segments.text: If the gap is real, our picture of the universe might be missing something. New physics, or a strange early dark energy.
segments.headline: New physics?

segments.text: It's one of the biggest open questions in science right now. Maybe someone watching will solve it.
segments.headline: Maybe you'll solve it
